title: Ordinary finite quotients and adic fibres of an integral constructible heart object
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale site put $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A/\varpi^n)_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $F$ be an object of the integral heart of [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure] in the completed constructible category with compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and regard $F$ as its degree-zero sheaf of $B_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $QF$ for its image under raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], with adic geometric fibres normalized as in [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres].

For each $n\ge1$, the ordinary sheaf quotient $F_n=F/\varpi^nF$ is canonically of etale origin: there is a constructible sheaf $G_n$ of $(A/\varpi^n)_T$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] with $\nu_T^*G_n\cong F_n$, where $\nu_T$ is the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The quotient maps give compatible transition maps $G_{n+1}\to G_n$ and $G_{n+1}/\varpi^nG_{n+1}\cong G_n$. There is one finite locally closed stratification of $T$ [def-constructible-stratification] on each stratum of which every $F_n$ is finite locally constant as a pro-etale sheaf and every $G_n$ is finite locally constant as an etale sheaf. Finite locally constant means locally isomorphic to a constant sheaf of a finite module.

For a geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], with etale stalks as in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], put $P_{\bar x}=\varprojlim_n(G_n)_{\bar x}$. This is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], the projections induce $P_{\bar x}/\varpi^nP_{\bar x}\cong(G_n)_{\bar x}$, and there is a natural isomorphism of adic coefficient fibres
$$(QF)_{\bar x}\cong P_{\bar x}\otimes_A E.$$
These identifications are natural in integral sheaf morphisms. In particular, if $u:B_T\to F$ is such a morphism, the induced maps $(A/\varpi^n)_T\to G_n$ are compatible and their values at $1$ determine $a_{\bar x}\in P_{\bar x}$; the fibre of $Qu$ sends $1$ to $a_{\bar x}\otimes1$. These are ordinary degree-zero quotients, not assertions that $F\otimes^L_{B_T}(A/\varpi^n)_T$ is concentrated in degree zero; torsion in the integral local models is allowed.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3) (integral heart and finite-module local models); Lemmas 5.1.2 and 5.1.4, Corollary 5.1.5 (finite discrete local systems and comparison); Lemma 6.8.2, Proposition 6.8.4(1), and Proposition 6.8.14(2) (completed/rational fibre normalization). The combined quotient and fibre comparison, including torsion local models, is agent-formulated from these results.

proof.text: The structure map $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite type. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the Noetherian one-point base, and [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] to its sole fibre, to obtain that $T$ is Noetherian and finite-dimensional. The unit $\ell\in k$ stays invertible in its local rings. By [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure], $F$ has only its degree-zero ambient cohomology. Apply condition (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] to this object. It gives one finite locally closed stratification, and on each stratum $S$ a pro-etale covering on which $F|_S$ is $B_S\otimes_A\underline N$ for a finitely presented $A$-module $N$. This covering and $N$ are chosen before $n$; $N$ need not be free.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); the completed-category local-model comparison is the cited characterization

proof.text: For the immersion $i:S\to T$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation] gives exact ordinary inverse image and preservation of the coefficient limit. The finite coefficient sheaves restrict to the same constant sheaves on $S$; hence $i^{-1}B_T=B_S$. For a pro-etale site object, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies restriction with the slice site and identifies constant coefficients. Limits are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]; the identical slice coverings show that both commute with this restriction. Thus the completed coefficients restrict to the same completed coefficients on the chart. Thus restricting an ordinary cokernel $F/\varpi^nF$ gives $(F|_S)/\varpi^n(F|_S)$, also after passing to the covering of Step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction], $B_S$ is flat over the constant $A$ and $B_S\otimes_A A/\varpi^n$ is the constant coefficient sheaf $(A/\varpi^n)_S$. All identifications use the quotient maps, so they commute with $n$ and multiplication by coefficients.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), Remark 6.8.15; Stacks sites-modules.tex Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat), proetale.tex Tag 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion)

proof.text:
On a chart with local model $B\otimes_A\underline N$, the balanced tensor relations give
$$ (B\otimes_A\underline N)/\varpi^n(B\otimes_A\underline N)\cong(B/\varpi^nB)\otimes_A\underline N\cong\underline{N/\varpi^nN}.$$
For the first map, send the class of $b\otimes m$ to $\bar b\otimes m$; its inverse sends $\bar b\otimes m$ to the class of $b\otimes m$, independent of the lift $b$. The second map follows from Step 2 and exactness of the constant-module functor [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties]. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] and [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], $A/\varpi^n$ is a finite ring. Since a finite generating set of $N$ gives a surjection $(A/\varpi^n)^r\to N/\varpi^nN$, its quotient is finite. Consequently all $F_n$ are finite locally constant on the single stratification in Step 1.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10; ordinary balanced tensor quotient computation and finite constant-module models

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-sheaf-origin] with the finite ring $A/\varpi^n$ to $F_n$. Take its canonical etale representative $G_n=\nu_{T,*}F_n$ with the comparison counit as isomorphism; this choice is justified by full faithfulness and essential image, and [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] identifies the unit with an isomorphism. To check the same strata, use [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]: $\nu_S^*(G_n|_S)\cong F_n|_S$. By [det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist], the latter has an etale finite locally constant representative on $S$. Full faithfulness at $S$ identifies this representative with $G_n|_S$. This proves constructibility of $G_n$ and finite local constancy on exactly the strata already chosen, for every $n$.

source.place: Stacks proetale.tex Tag 09AK (lemma-compare-constructible) and Tag 099Y (lemma-compare-locally-constant); comparison restriction compatibility

proof.text:
The quotient $F_{n+1}\to F_n$ is linear over $A/\varpi^{n+1}$, with $F_n$ regarded by restriction of scalars. Both have etale origin. Full faithfulness from [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] lifts it uniquely to $G_{n+1}\to G_n$; uniqueness gives every transition-composition equation. The identity
$$ (F/\varpi^{n+1}F)/\varpi^n(F/\varpi^{n+1}F)=F/\varpi^nF $$
is the ordinary quotient identity: both quotient maps have kernel $\varpi^nF$ because $\varpi^{n+1}F\subseteq\varpi^nF$. Exactness of $\nu_T^*$ in the same cited proposition carries $G_{n+1}/\varpi^nG_{n+1}$ to this quotient. Full faithfulness reflects its canonical map to $G_n$ as an isomorphism. This also proves the quotient cocycle; no derived concentration assertion was used.

source.place: Finite-level comparison and the elementary iterated ordinary quotient identity

proof.text: Fix $\bar x$. By [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], the transitions of $M_n=(G_n)_{\bar x}$ induce $M_{n+1}/\varpi^nM_{n+1}\cong M_n$. These modules are finite: restrict to its stratum using [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar], then use an etale trivializing neighbourhood and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk]. Apply [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules](1) to this normalized tower. It gives that $P_{\bar x}=\varprojlim_nM_n$ is finitely generated over $A$ and that its projection induces $P_{\bar x}/\varpi^nP_{\bar x}\cong M_n$, including possible torsion. These are the projection-induced maps, not arbitrarily chosen module isomorphisms.

source.place: Stacks algebra.tex Tags 09B8 (lemma-limit-complete) and 031D (lemma-finite-over-complete-ring); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact)

proof.text: Here is the fibre comparison with torsion retained until rationalization. At $\bar x$ choose a geometric lift to a chart of Step 1. The stalk comparisons [lem-cbc-proetale-comparison-stalk] and [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-stalk], followed by [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk], identify the entire finite tower $M_n$ with $(N/\varpi^nN)_n$. By [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules](2), its limit is $N$ via the residue maps. Under [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], $QF$ on this chart is $E_S\otimes_A N$. Choose a finite presentation $A^a\xrightarrow{D}A^b\to N\to0$. The normalized adic fibre of the free coefficient modules is $E^a,E^b$, and the constant matrix $D$ induces the same matrix over $E$, by the finite-level normalization of [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres]. Exactness of its fibre functor identifies the fibre of the cokernel with $\operatorname{coker}(D:E^a\to E^b)=N\otimes_AE$, the last equality being [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]. Together with $P_{\bar x}\cong N$, this gives $(QF)_{\bar x}\cong P_{\bar x}\otimes_AE$. The map sends each generator to the tensor of its compatible residue classes. Therefore changing a presentation or a trivializing chart gives the same map, since those generators still have the same residues; it is the canonical coefficient comparison. This calculation kills torsion only after tensoring with $E$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2, Definition 6.8.10, Propositions 6.8.11(3) and 6.8.14(2); finite-presentation computation with the normalized exact adic fibre

proof.text: All constructions are functorial in an integral morphism: take ordinary quotients, apply the fully faithful comparison of Step 4, take etale stalks, then inverse limits and tensor with $E$. The comparisons of Step 7 use these same quotient maps and are natural, as are rational realization and the normalized fibre functor in [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] and [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres]. For the source $B_T$, Step 2 gives the constant system $(A/\varpi^n)_T$, and its fibre limit is $A$ by [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules](2). Thus $u:B_T\to F$ gives compatible maps $(A/\varpi^n)_T\to G_n$. Their stalk values $a_n$ at $1$ satisfy $a_{n+1}\bmod\varpi^n=a_n$, so they define $a_{\bar x}=(a_n)_n\in P_{\bar x}$. Tensoring the resulting map $A\to P_{\bar x}$ with $E$ sends $1$ to $a_{\bar x}\otimes1$, which is the fibre of $Qu$ by naturality. All quotients above were ordinary cokernels.

source.place: Canonical quotient, inverse-limit, and localization maps in Lemma 6.8.2 and Propositions 6.8.4(1), 6.8.14(2)
